# The Run File {#sec-file-format}

A run is one HDF5 file. Its geometry follows VTK's **VTKHDF** layout for
temporal `PolyData`, so ParaView and VTK ≥ 9.3 (`vtkHDFReader`, and with it
PyVista) open it directly: every recorded frame is one time step, and the
number of points and triangles may change from step to step (remeshing).
Everything else lives in the sibling group `/DropletRelaxer`, which VTK
ignores. The file is written with plain `h5py`; no VTK is needed on the
machine that runs the solver.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from DropletRelaxer.io import schema

print("```text")
print(schema.__doc__.split("\n\n", 1)[1].rstrip())
print("```\n")
print(f"Current format: `format_version = {schema.FORMAT_VERSION}`, "
      f"VTKHDF version {'.'.join(map(str, schema.VTKHDF_VERSION))}.\n")
```

## Per-frame arrays

Generated from `DropletRelaxer.io.schema`, which the writer, the reader and
the tests share.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from DropletRelaxer.io import schema

print(schema.markdown_table())
```

## Writing and reading while a run is in progress

All datasets are chunked and resizable and are created when the run starts;
then the file switches to HDF5 SWMR (single writer, multiple readers) mode. A
frame is appended data first; `Steps/Values` and the `Steps/NSteps` attribute
are updated last, and readers count frames by them, so they never see a
half-written frame. `DropletRelaxer.io.reader.RunFile` with `follow=True`
(what `droplet-view --follow` uses) refreshes and picks up new frames.

The file is written in the HDF5 1.10 format, the oldest that supports SWMR,
so that the HDF5 library bundled with VTK can read it.

## Restart checkpoints

`/DropletRelaxer/checkpoint` has two slots. The writer fills the slot that is
not current and switches the `current` attribute only afterwards, so a run
killed while writing a checkpoint still has the previous one. A checkpoint
holds the mesh and the complete loop state of the driver (remesh bookkeeping,
quasi-static controller), which is why a restart is bit-identical to an
uninterrupted run. On restart, frames and events recorded after the
checkpoint are dropped and written again.

## Reading a run file in Python

```python
from DropletRelaxer.io.reader import RunFile

with RunFile("run.h5") as rf:
    s = rf.series()                 # per-frame scalars as arrays: energy, force (N, 3), ...
    last = rf.frame(-1)             # a Frame: verts, tris, boundary_idx, curvature, ...
    cfg, table = rf.config()        # the scenario as given
```
